title: Staggered reopen backoff and eviction coordinator hotfix for cross-region graceful drain
author: Evan Cho
description:
Context: During a recent regional maintenance window we observed a cascading spike in circuit transitions and an elevated error rate while nodes were draining KV caches. The root cause traced to two races: (1) circuits that were reopened immediately after a short cooldown when a partially drained KV cache still returned cache-miss latencies, causing rapid reopen/close churn; (2) eviction/drain signals were not coordinated with the scheduler's soft-eviction path, so requests were occasionally routed to nodes mid-drain leading to tail latency and increased 5xx counts.

What this PR does: Implements a staggered reopen backoff with tenant-scoped jitter and an eviction coordinator handshake to ensure KV cache drain completes before a node is re-advertised for normal traffic. The patch is deliberately narrow and labeled as a hotfix: it focuses on safe defaults and observability to reduce blast radius.

Design highlights: - Staggered reopen backoff: new backoff policy with exponential base, per-tenant seedable jitter, and a configurable max cap. This prevents synchronized reopen storms when many circuits flip at once. - Eviction coordinator: a lightweight gRPC control-plane signal that makes drains explicit. Nodes publish drain phase states (prepare -> draining -> complete). The scheduler honors 'draining' by avoiding routing new long-running requests and by triggering hard-prefetch of KV prefixes to minimize mid-request misses. - KV drain handshake: coordination between eviction_coordinator and kv_drain to ensure the cache flush/sync completes before node becomes schedulable again. - Observability: adds metric 'circuit.reopen_reason' (labels: tenant, region, reason) and tracing tag 'eviction.phase' to help root-cause future incidents. - Safe defaults: feature-gated at runtime with cluster-level opt-in; default settings are conservative for the hosted platform.

Why this is a hotfix: We saw this exact pattern during an ops-driven node drain where the combination of fast reopen and uncoordinated drains produced visible SLO regressions. The changes are backward-compatible (new handshake is optional/timeboxed) and guarded behind a single runtime flag so we can roll-forward or disable quickly.

Testing performed: - Unit tests for backoff math and jitter distribution (deterministic seeds). - Integration test simulating node drain + cross-region traffic with mock KV backend included in integration/tests/drain_e2e_test.go. - Canary rollout in staging with 3 customers reproduced previous failure mode and confirmed latency and 5xx rates stayed within SLO bounds. - Manual chaos run: concurrent tenant spikes while draining produced no reopen storm after the change.

CI history: initial push failed flaky TestSchedulerRace in integration; fixed by adding a deterministic drain timeout and re-ran CI. Final CI: all checks passing (unit, lint, integration).

Rollout plan: 1) Merge to main behind runtime flag. 2) Deploy to staging with flag enabled for 24 hours and run smoke + load tests. 3) Enable in a selected set of low-latency customers in hosted for 48h with enhanced monitoring dashboards. 4) Gradually enable globally if no regressions.

Rollback: disable runtime flag to revert behavior instantly. If deeper rollback required, revert the merge and redeploy; changes are isolated to runtime path and do not modify persisted schemas.

Notes / alternatives considered: - Full scheduler rewrite to make drains atomic (too large/risky for hotfix). - Global randomized reopen window (rejected because it lacks tenant granularity and makes debugging harder).

Related: ENG-5421 (SLO degradation investigation), ENG-5482 (regional drain postmortem).

Author response: added metric + seedable jitter, documented cap rationale in comments and docs.

release_notes: Hotfix: reduce circuit flip storms during node drains by adding staggered reopen backoff and coordianted KV drain handshake; new observability to help diagnose reopen causes.
